interpretation.observation_fit: Full-pose achieves 0.17 px vs 0.41 px constrained — it fits corners better, as expected with more parameters (132 vs 87).
interpretation.baseline: Constrained=16.8mm, Full=27.8mm → different by 11.0mm. Poses and rayfield compensate strongly.
interpretation.convergence: Constrained=15.0°, Full=25.3° → substantial redistribution between poses and rayfield.
interpretation.dy_range: Constrained=0.0552, Full=0.1905 → full-pose has 3.5× larger direction variation, less telecentric.
interpretation.asymmetry: Constrained X asymmetry=0.965mm, Full=4.986mm → full-pose is 5× less symmetric. Whether the real microscope IS symmetric is unknown.
interpretation.theta_field: Constrained θ range across FOV=0.38°, Full=1.24° → full-pose convergence varies 3× more spatially.
interpretation.pose_rotation: Full-pose RMS rotation variation across frames=0.72°. This 0.72° of per-frame tilt is absorbed by the rayfield in the constrained model.
interpretation.key_finding: The choice of pose model STRONGLY changes the inferred rayfield geometry. This is a pose/rayfield identifiability issue — without external ground truth, we cannot claim either variant is physically correct.
interpretation.recommendation: The constrained Zernike is the more CONSERVATIVE intermediate for CMO-like interpretation (more symmetric, more telecentric). The full-pose Zernike fits the observations better but yields a less regular rayfield. Neither is proven 'correct' — they represent different points on the bias-variance tradeoff of the inverse problem.
